strategy.summary: Small family-owned sheet-metal shop and the single source for the welded, painted base frame part:330010 under framework ctr:4600070310. We own the tooling. Its delivery and quality are poor and getting worse: scorecard red, on-time delivery around 63 %, ppm about nine times the peer median and rising. It has signalled a cash need by asking for payment within 10 days against a cash discount. Its renewal history is habitual: it asks for a small increase and settles at zero or below. Steel and labour indices give it a real but modest cost argument, and power is falling. We matter to it at about 11 % of its turnover. Leverage leans our way, but single sourcing and fragile delivery mean we should trade (fast payment, binding volume, 24 months) for price stability and a binding ppm/OTD commitment, not squeeze. There is no should-cost, so margin evidence is thin.
strategy.decision_maker: Likely the owner/managing director of a small family GmbH with a short approval path. No named contact appears in the evidence.

persona.style: Pragmatic small-shop seller. It asks modestly, settles low and is cash-minded; it is currently on the defensive about quality.

price_view.reasoning: There is no should-cost. Drivers point to a small increase: steel and labour up, power down, with a third of the cost unexplained. History shows it settles at zero or below its ask. Poor performance justifies holding the current price, and fast payment plus volume could buy a small cut. A deep cut is unrealistic and risky.

findings.text: No should-cost, no quotes and no RFQ data exist for part:330010, so how far the price sits above full cost cannot be measured. Price room can only be judged from index drivers and the price history. The evidence is thin on margin.
The weighted drivers support a moderate increase of about +2.6% over 12 months: steel +2.09%, labour +0.77% and power -0.22%. The drivers cover only 67% of the cost; the other 33% is unexplained.

The price has been flat at 100.14 since 2024, after a cut of 6% from 106.55. Since the 2024 reset, steel first fell to a low in 2025-11 and has since risen 7.8%. Steel is still 6.3% below its 2023-08 peak, when the price was 106.55. Cumulative driver pressure since the last price change is therefore modest. The peak comparisons are not checkable, so they should be used only as context.

The price is fixed for each calendar year, and any change needs 90 days' notice before year end, i.e. by about 2026-10-02. A request for 2027 is imminent. In past renewals the supplier asked for +1.2% on average and settled at -2.0%; the last renewal asked +3.6% and settled at 0%.

Performance argues against any increase. The scorecard is red: 63% on time against a peer median of 84.6%, and 4118 ppm against a peer median of 457 (1871 a year ago). There were 7 complaints on the part, and the defect cost belongs in our total cost.

The supplier wants cash: it asked us to pay within 10 days in exchange for a cash discount. It is also exposed to us, since we account for 11.3% of its turnover. Its equity ratio of 24.1% is moderate. A trade of faster payment for a held or lower price is feasible. One caveat: we currently pay late on average.

findings.text: Small family-owned sheet-metal shop (founded 1982, 70 staff, ~EUR 7.5 M turnover). Decisions likely sit with the owner/managing director, with a short approval path. The evidence names no person and contains no call or meeting notes, so the persona picture is thin.

Cash need is the clearest signal. On 2026-09-11 they asked us to pay invoices within 10 days in exchange for a cash discount. Their equity ratio of 24.1% is modest, while the credit index of 232 has been stable for 12 months, so this looks like no acute distress. A faster-payment-for-discount or price trade is the most attractive currency we have.

Our payment record is a sensitivity they can use. We are already late on 94.7% of invoices, by 6.1 days on average and at most 17 days, against 45-day net terms, and we have never taken a discount. They may raise this. Fixing our own payment discipline is a cheap gesture.

Their performance position is weak. Our Supplier Quality letter of 2026-09-24 puts their scorecard at red: 63% on-time delivery and 4118 ppm, against a peer median of 84.6% on-time and 457 ppm. Their ppm has risen from 1871 a year earlier. Part 330010 had 7 complaints, and 1 of them lacks a closed 8D. We have demanded a binding improvement plan and cost recovery, which gives us strong moral leverage. Their only positive is a renewed ISO 9001 certificate.

We matter to them: our spend is about 11.3% of their turnover, and our volume is growing from 8500 to 8980 units. Historically they settle well below their ask; in the last renewal they asked +3.6% and settled at 0%. The price has been frozen at 100.14 since 2024.
Our constraint is that they are the single approved source for part 330010. We own the tooling and can exit the contract by giving notice before 2027-04-01, so a move is credible but slow.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070310 covers only part:330010 (Base frame HN 50/65), runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and extends automatically by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice is due by 2027-04-01, so we still hold a credible exit.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end (by about 2026-10-02 for 2027). A late or informal increase request has no contractual footing for 1 Jan 2027.

Payment terms are 45 days net, shorter than our 60-day standard, so this is already a benefit to the supplier. Delivery is DAP with a 21-day lead time. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a flat EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint, a low recovery rate.

The supplier has settled well below its ask in every renewal: -2.2 asked, -6 settled (2024); +2.2 asked, 0 settled (2025); +3.6 asked, 0 settled (2026). The price has been flat at 100.14 since 2024, down 6% from 106.55, so a zero settlement is its usual outcome.

Dependency runs both ways. The supplier is our single source at 100% quota, approved since 2021. We own the tooling, so the part can be moved. Our spend of about EUR 851k is about 11.3% of its EUR 7.5M turnover, which makes us an important customer.

Its performance is weak. The scorecard is red: 63% on time and 4118 ppm, against a peer median of 457 ppm. Supplier Quality has formally demanded an improvement plan. Its financials are only moderate (equity ratio 24.1%, VDA 6.3 audit grade C).

findings.text: Delivery is chronically poor and not improving: rolling OTD 63.0% (target 95%, peer median 84.6%), stuck between 62% and 70% for two years. In the last 12 months 29.6% of receipts were late, averaging 9.8 days and up to 20 days late. Confirmed dates equal requested dates, so it confirms what it then misses. There were 7 rush lines and 10 partial lines on top.

Quality is deteriorating sharply. Rolling ppm rose from 1197 (2025Q4) to 4118 (2026Q3), about 9x the peer median of 457, and the score fell to 60.9, class C red. Complaint quantity per notification is rising: 8, 5, 8, 7 pieces per lot in 2026 against 1-3 earlier. Defects recur: leakage at test, surface damage, coating, burr, missing marking. 20 of 22 notifications are supplier-caused.

Defect cost recovery is weak. Only EUR 1,650 has been recharged over 22 notifications; the EUR 150 flat fee was charged on only about half of the supplier-caused cases. 8D closure takes about 2-3 months, and qn:20005001 has no closed 8D yet. Our Supplier Quality letter of 2026-09-24 already demands an improvement plan and cost recovery.

Volume outlook is stable to slightly up and shared with the supplier: 8,980 pcs forecast for the next 12 months against 8,500 ordered. Monthly demand is uneven, with a dip of 250 in 2027-08 and 490 in 2026-12. At 100.14 EUR this is about EUR 0.9 M a year, roughly 11-12% of its turnover; this volume is our lever.
Price has been flat at 100.14 since 2024, down 6% from 106.55. This supports its case that it has already conceded. The steel and labour indices also favour it at about +2-3% on price.

Our own conduct gives it counterarguments. We pay 94.7% of invoices late, by 6.1 days on average. The single-source position for part:330010 limits our ability to switch quickly, although we own the tooling.

arguments.text: Our price has been frozen at EUR 100.14 for three calendar years (2024, 2025, 2026) after we gave a 6 % cut, while steel and labour rose. A modest increase for 2027 is overdue, not opportunistic.

Our cost drivers have risen. Basic iron and steel is +6.5 % over 12 months, with a weight of about 32 %. Manufacturing labour is +2.7 %, with a weight of about 29 %. Weighted, that is roughly +2.9 % on cost before power. Power is down 3.7 %, but it is only 6 % of our cost.

Hollerau pays late as a habit: 94.7 % of invoices arrive late, on average 6 days past the 45-day term. That is effectively financing at our expense for a small family firm. We ask for 10-day payment against a cash discount.
We are the only approved source and have been since 2021. Requalifying a welded, painted frame elsewhere costs time and risk. Continuity with us is worth something.

Hollerau's demand fluctuates, which makes capacity planning hard and contributes to late deliveries. There were 7 rush lines and changed lines. Forecast swings run from 8,410 to 10,050 per year, and the monthly forecast ranges from 250 to 1,000 pieces.

weak_points: Our quality is bad and getting worse: 4,118 ppm over 12 months, a red scorecard and a formal escalation letter. Leakage and surface-damage lots of 7-8 pieces in 2026 alone.
On-time delivery is 63 %, against a contractual target of 95 %. The rush-order excuse is thin because confirmed dates equal requested dates.
The contract fixes the price per calendar year and requires 90 days' written notice before year end. That deadline is 2 October, and we may have missed it for 2027.
Hollerau owns the tooling, so moving the part is easier than we would like.
Our history shows we always settle at zero. They expect us to fold again.
We have a thin equity ratio of 24 %, and our cash request reveals need.
Hollerau is about 11 % of our turnover. Losing them would hurt us far more than it hurts them.
8D closures take 2-3 months. One QN, from August 2026, is still open.
wants: Payment in 10 days, or at least strictly 30 days and paid on time, in exchange for a 2 % cash discount or a price hold.
A binding annual volume of around 9,000 pieces with a smoothed call-off schedule.
Extension to 24 or 36 months, beyond June 2027.
A steel index clause on the roughly 32 % material share instead of a frozen fixed price.
A realistic ppm and OTD ramp-up plan rather than immediate punitive chargebacks. Keep the chargeback at EUR 150 flat.
red_lines: No price cut below EUR 100.14 without fast payment and binding volume in return.
No uncapped chargebacks or high per-complaint fees that would wipe out our margin.
No commitment to 95 % OTD or a 1,000-ppm target immediately. A phased plan only.
No shortening of the 21-day lead time without a buffer stock that Hollerau pays for.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long cooperation and take the escalation seriously. Commit to submitting an improvement plan for frame HN 50/65, with welding/leak-test and packaging measures, within 4 weeks. Then point out that the price has been unchanged at EUR 100.14 since 2024 after our 6 % cut, while steel rose 6.5 % and labour 2.7 %. Propose +3.5 % for 2027, or alternatively price stability if Hollerau moves to 10-day payment with a cash discount and a 24-month binding volume of about 9,000 pieces per year. Signal readiness to discuss a steel index clause.

rebuttals.answer: We acknowledge that the price has been stable since the last renewal and that steel and labour have moved up since then. Stability was the outcome both sides agreed at each renewal, and the current price is the clear anchor for any discussion. Over the same period delivery and quality have fallen well short of the agreement, so a fair review for next year has to weigh performance alongside cost. We are open to discussing price stability as part of a package that also secures a binding improvement in quality and delivery.

Your steel and labour figures match the indices we track, and we accept that they point to some cost pressure. Weighted by their share of cost, they support only a modest effect on the price, not a broad increase. Power has fallen and offsets part of it. The rest of the cost base has no shown driver. Taken in proportion, the evidence supports a small adjustment at most, and the quality costs we currently absorb more than offset it.

You are right that our payments have regularly arrived a few days after the due date, and we will correct that; on-time payment is a commitment we are ready to make. We also take your request for faster payment against a cash discount seriously. We would prefer to build it into the unit price of a renewed agreement rather than handle it invoice by invoice, so you get reliable cash and we both get a clean price.

We value the long relationship and agree that continuity has worth for both sides. Continuity rests on dependable supply, though, and at present a large share of deliveries are late and the defect rate is far above peers. The tooling is ours and the framework sets clear targets. Our preference is to stay with you, on the basis of a credible improvement plan rather than a price premium for being the single source.

Some monthly variation in our call-offs is real, and we are happy to improve how we share it. But the forecast has been shared with you throughout, the annual volume has stayed within a narrow band, and the next year's outlook is above what we ordered last year. Your own confirmed dates match our requested dates, so lateness against your own confirmations cannot come from our planning. A binding volume and a longer term would give you the planning certainty you ask for.

press: We would welcome your improvement plan for the base frame, including a ppm level you can commit to for the next contract period, since the recent leakage and surface-damage lots have hit our assembly hard.
As your confirmed delivery dates match our requested dates, could you explain what will lift on-time delivery toward the contractual target?
Could you confirm whether formal written notice of a price change for next year was sent within the period set in our framework agreement?
We are prepared to offer faster payment, a binding volume and a longer term, and would like to understand how you would reflect that in the unit price.
